newsitem.title: UK: TV dispute might delay Formula One float - paper.
newsitem.headline: TV dispute might delay Formula One float - paper.

text.p: A legal dispute in Germany over television rights could delay the flotation of the world's most glamorous and expensive motor racing event -- Formula One.

The Times newspaper reported in its Monday edition that the dispute, the latest threat to a sale that has been estimated to be worth $2.5-3.3 billion, looked unlikely to be resolved in time to allow the float to proceed next month.
Quoting an insider, the Times said: "We are on track to go ahead before the British Grand Prix at Silverstone on July 13, although it is possible the timing could shift."

Formula One, which is owned by multi-millionaire Bernie Ecclestone and whose racing teams include Williams, Benetton, Jordan, Tyrell and McLaren, has said that the flotation is complex and any timetable is provisional.
The company's investment bankers meet on Monday, the Times reported.
